extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from local XML/PDF/OA material; no unsupported direct mechanism claim is promoted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The article frames BMAP-27/BMAP-28 antimicrobial action as rapid binding to and permeabilization of target microorganism membranes, but this paper uses that as cited mechanism context rather than a newly quantified direct mechanism assay.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: BMAP-27, BMAP-28, and synthetic analogs discussed in this paper
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism statement is background/interpretive context supported by cited prior work; final activity claims are based on MIC/antiviral/in vivo efficacy tables.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Truncation or hydrophilic substitution of the hydrophobic C-terminal region changes Gram-positive/Gram-negative activity and mammalian toxicity, supporting a source-reviewed SAR caution that the C-terminal tail contributes to toxicity and in vivo efficacy.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: BMAP-27(1–18), BMAP-28(1–18), BMAP-28(10–27), and mBMAP-28 compared with parent BMAPs
mechanism_claims.limitations: Phenotypic SAR evidence; not a direct molecular target or binding-site assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The study does not support broad antiviral efficacy: BMAP-28 shows partial HSV-1 protection/yield inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentration, while BMAP-27 toxicity and lack of PRCV activity limit antiviral conclusions.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: BMAP-28 antiviral result and negative/limited antiviral findings
mechanism_claims.limitations: Antiviral activity is phenotype-only and not a viral mechanism-of-action assay.
